title: Install DiaTweaks
text: A few steps in Terminal. After that, make it yours in Settings. > Before you begin: DiaTweaks is unofficial and supports Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later. It modifies a copy of Dia, including its signature. Read the steps below before installing. Install 1. Put Dia in your Applications folder. 2. Install Apple's developer tools: xcode-select --install 3. Paste this into Terminal: sh git clone https://github.com/JaceThings/DiaTweaks.git ~/DiaTweaks && ~/DiaTweaks/install.sh Dia quits and reopens. If macOS asks about "Dia Safe Storage", enter your password and click Always Allow. Choose your first tweak Open Dia → Settings → Patches. Every tweak has its own switch, preview, and wiki page. Start with the Coming from Arc guide, or browse all tweaks. Password managers Apple Passwords, its passkeys, and 1Password need the matching tweak enabled in the Passwords section. These are off by default. Read Allow iCloud Passkeys or Allow 1Password before relying on them. If something feels wrong See updates and recovery for restoring the original app and troubleshooting.

title: A familiar place to start.
text: You don't have to leave every habit behind. DiaTweaks brings familiar interactions to Dia, one switch at a time. Start with your browser Install Dia and use its own import and setup tools for your browsing data. DiaTweaks customizes Dia; it does not transfer your Arc account, Spaces, extensions, or saved tabs. Keep a copy of anything you need from Arc before changing your setup. Find the things you miss In Arc In DiaTweaks What to expect --- --- --- Peek Peek on Shift-Click Shift-click a link for a preview over your page. Escape closes it; ⌘O keeps it as a tab. Little Arc Little Dia Open links from other apps in a small window. Enable it, then relaunch Dia. A quieter toolbar Hide Toolbar Give the page more room. This tweak is experimental; pair it with Show Toolbar on Hover. A command bar over the page Open New Tabs in Command Bar Open the command bar without leaving the page you're on. Collapsible pinned tabs Collapse Pinned Tabs Fold pinned tabs under a Pinned line. A shortcut to pin a tab Pin Tab Shortcut Use ⌘D to pin the current tab. These are individual tweaks, not a complete recreation of Arc. Read each page for options, dependencies, and limitations. Make one change at a time After installation, open Dia → Settings → Patches. Pick one tweak, read its preview and instructions, and switch it on. Most changes apply immediately; some ask you to relaunch. If you prefer Terminal, run diatweaks for an interactive menu, or diatweaks list to see which tweaks are enabled. You can use the Settings interface for everyday changes. Keep a way back DiaTweaks keeps an untouched copy of Dia. To return to the original browser, open Settings → Home → Restore…, or run diatweaks restore. Your guide to updates and recovery covers what changes after installation.

title: The command-line guide
text: Prefer Terminal? Every tweak is a command away. Run diatweaks on its own for a menu, or: Command Does ------ diatweaks list Shows every tweak and whether it's on diatweaks enable hideToolbar Turns tweaks on; Dia changes straight away diatweaks disable hideToolbar Turns tweaks off diatweaks status Shows Dia's version, safe mode and which tweaks are on diatweaks update Installs the latest DiaTweaks release and patches Dia again diatweaks update-dia Downloads a newer Dia and patches it diatweaks restore Puts the original Dia back Tweak names work as keys or titles, like hideToolbar or "Hide Toolbar", and enable and disable take several at once. Add -y to skip the questions.

title: Updates & recovery
text: Keep your setup current, and know how to get back to the original Dia. Updating Dia's own updater is switched off. Settings → Home → Software Update checks for a new Dia and a new DiaTweaks release, downloads either one, and relaunches Dia to install it, like macOS's Software Update. Under Automatic Updates, pick for each of Dia and DiaTweaks: off, just show updates, download them, or download and install them when you quit (the default). A DiaTweaks you built from source with install.sh is never downloaded or replaced automatically: Update Now or diatweaks update installs the latest release, and automatic updates apply from then on. - Dia now: diatweaks update-dia - DiaTweaks now: diatweaks update Installed before diatweaks existed? Update once by hand, then use diatweaks update from then on: sh rm -rf /tmp/DiaTweaks && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/JaceThings/DiaTweaks.git /tmp/DiaTweaks && /tmp/DiaTweaks/install.sh Questions & troubleshooting Is it safe? It's built on your Mac from this code, and it doesn't send anything about you anywhere. It goes online only to check for updates and to load the preview pictures in Settings. A few tweaks look at what's in Dia to work: Group Tabs by Domain reads your tabs' addresses, and Tidy Tabs gives your tab titles and addresses to Apple's on-device model, which runs on your Mac. The password tweaks pass messages between your password manager and its extension without reading them. How does it work? It keeps an untouched copy of Dia and makes a second copy that loads a small add-on. The add-on changes parts of Dia while it runs. When Dia updates, DiaTweaks patches the new version the same way. Why does my Mac ask about "Dia Safe Storage"? The tweaked Dia is signed by you instead of The Browser Company, so macOS checks once per Dia update. Click Always Allow. Why does screen sharing ask for permission again? macOS ties Screen Recording to the app's signature, and the tweaked Dia is signed differently from the original. The first time DiaTweaks patches Dia (and when it goes back to the original), it clears the old permission so macOS asks once for the new one. Switch on Dia under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording, then quit and reopen Dia. Dia and DiaTweaks updates keep your permission. If sharing still loops, run tccutil reset ScreenCapture company.thebrowser.dia and try again. Does it run in the background? No. It only does anything while Dia is open. Does anything stop working? Apple Passwords, its passkeys and 1Password only trust the original Dia, so in the patched one they stop working until you switch on the matching tweak in the Passwords section. Those run the original Dia without windows as a go-between, which is why they're off by default. How it works → What if Dia keeps crashing? If Dia crashes twice in a row right after opening, it opens next time with the tweaks off. Settings → Patches has a button to turn them back on. Restore the original Dia In Dia, open Settings → Home and click Restore…. Dia reopens as the original app with its own updates. To also delete DiaTweaks' files and the diatweaks command, run diatweaks restore --purge instead.

title: Built in the open.
text: DiaTweaks is maintained by Jace and its contributors. The wiki, previews, code, and this website are public. Improve the documentation Found an unclear explanation? Suggest a change in the upstream repository, and link the wiki page. The wiki is the source of truth; this website renders a versioned snapshot of it. Make a tweak Start with Discoveries to learn how Dia is built. Then read the project's contribution guide for patch structure, tests, and pull request requirements. Improve this website The website lives in website/ in the repository. It builds to static HTML and runs on GitHub Pages. See the website README for local development and wiki synchronization. Independent by design DiaTweaks is unofficial and is not affiliated with The Browser Company. Dia and Arc belong to their respective owners.

title: Edge-to-Edge Web Pages
text: Dia leaves a thin gap between the page and the edges of the window. This tweak removes it, so the page reaches the edges. Vertical tabs Horizontal tabs :---::---: Why use it Dia pads the page with a few pixels of window color on every side. That strip wastes room and makes the page look like a floating card. - If you want more of the screen for the page, or a cleaner look, switch it on. - Skip it if you like the framed look Dia ships with. Turn it on It's on by default. Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Edge-to-Edge Web Pages. Or run: sh diatweaks enable edgeToEdge Options On the same page, once it's on: - Square Corners Next to Sidebar gives the page straight edges where it meets the sidebar. It's on by default. FAQ Why is the gap back when Chat is open? With Chat open, Dia shows the page as a card next to it. Edge-to-edge steps aside until you close Chat. What happens in full screen? The page reaches the edges of the screen, and its corners there are square.

title: Square Corners Next to Sidebar
text: Dia rounds all four corners of the page, even the two next to the sidebar. This tweak makes those two square, so the page meets the sidebar in a straight line. Why use it With the page running to the window edge, rounded corners at the sidebar leave small wedges of background. Square corners there make the page and sidebar meet cleanly. - Handy if you use tabs in the sidebar and want a tidy seam. - Switch it off if you prefer all four corners rounded. Turn it on It's on by default. Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Edge-to-Edge Web Pages and switch on Square Corners Next to Sidebar. Or run: sh diatweaks enable squareSidebarCorners Needs Edge-to-Edge Web Pages. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable squareSidebarCorners offers to turn it on too. FAQ Why don't I see a difference? It only changes the corners next to the sidebar. With tabs at the top, the sidebar hidden or Chat open, it leaves the corners alone.

title: Hide Toolbar
text: Hides the bar above the page with the address, navigation buttons and extensions, and moves the page up into its place. It's experimental. Why use it The toolbar takes a strip of height from every page, and you may rarely use it if you open sites from the command bar or the sidebar. - If you want the most page possible, or a focused, Arc-like window, hide it. - Pair it with the options below so the toolbar comes back when you need the address. - It's experimental, so skip it if you click the toolbar's buttons all day. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Toolbar. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideToolbar Options On the same page, once it's on: Showing the Toolbar - Show Toolbar on Hover shows the toolbar while the pointer is at the top of the page. - Show Toolbar on New Tabs keeps it on new tab pages. - Show Toolbar with Sidebar shows it while the sidebar is open. - Toggle toolbar visibility hides or shows it with a shortcut, ⌃D unless you set another. Copying the URL - Show Toast When Copying URL shows a small Copied message after ⇧⌘C. - Show Toolbar When Copying URL shows the toolbar for a moment after ⇧⌘C. While It's Hidden - Show Loading Progress shows Dia's loading glow along the top of the page. It's on by default. - Hide Site Color in Tab Bar keeps the selected tab at the top in the page's color. Works with - Command bar opens ⌘L's bar over the page, where a new tab's opens, while the toolbar is hidden. - Hide Sidebar Button and Hide Chat Button are greyed out in Settings while this is on, because their buttons are hidden with the toolbar. FAQ Where did the bookmarks bar go? Dia puts it right under the toolbar, so it hides too. With Show Toolbar on Hover, it comes back with the toolbar. Can I still click at the top of the page? Yes. The hidden toolbar doesn't take clicks, so the top of the page works as usual.

title: Show Toolbar on Hover
text: With Hide Toolbar on, move the pointer to the very top of the page and the toolbar fades in over it. It hides again when the pointer moves away. Pointer away Pointer at the top :---::---: _Screenshot coming soon._ _Screenshot coming soon._ Why use it Hiding the toolbar leaves no way to see the address or reach its buttons with the mouse. This brings it back on demand without taking space. - Use it if you hide the toolbar but still want the address bar one flick away. - It's the choice for tabs at the top, where there's no sidebar to open. - Leave it off if you keep brushing the top edge and the toolbar keeps popping up. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Hide Toolbar and, under Showing the Toolbar, switch on Show Toolbar on Hover. Or run: sh diatweaks enable revealToolbarOnHover Needs Hide Toolbar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable revealToolbarOnHover offers to turn it on too. FAQ Does the page jump when the toolbar shows? No. The toolbar shows on top of the page, so the page stays where it is. When does it hide again? A moment after the pointer leaves it. It stays while you type in the address bar or hold the mouse button down, and hides at once when you switch to another window or app. Why doesn't it show in some windows? It only works in the window you're using, while Dia is the active app.

title: Show Toolbar on New Tabs
text: With Hide Toolbar on, new tab pages keep the toolbar and the bookmarks bar, so you can click a bookmark or type an address straight away. Once a site opens, they hide again. Tabs in the sidebar Tabs at the top :---::---: Why use it A new tab page is where you type an address or pick a bookmark, and both are in the toolbar. Without it you'd have to reveal the toolbar first. - Handy if you start most browsing from a blank tab. - Skip it if you open new tabs with the command bar instead. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Hide Toolbar and, under Showing the Toolbar, switch on Show Toolbar on New Tabs. Or run: sh diatweaks enable showToolbarOnNewTab Needs Hide Toolbar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable showToolbarOnNewTab offers to turn it on too. FAQ Does the bookmarks bar show too? Yes, if Dia shows it (View → Show Bookmarks Bar). It stays with the toolbar. Does it work with tabs at the top? Yes. It only depends on whether the tab you're on is a new tab page.

title: Show Toolbar with Sidebar
text: With Hide Toolbar on, open the sidebar and the toolbar comes back, so you can see and type in the address bar. Close the sidebar and it hides again. Sidebar closed Sidebar open :---::---: _Screenshot coming soon._ _Screenshot coming soon._ Why use it When you open the sidebar you're usually navigating, so the address bar is useful there. This shows it for exactly that time and hides it the rest of the time. - Handy if you keep the sidebar closed while reading and open it to switch or search. - It does nothing with tabs at the top. Use Show Toolbar with Tabs at the Top or Show Toolbar on Hover there. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Hide Toolbar and, under Showing the Toolbar, switch on Show Toolbar with Sidebar. Or run: sh diatweaks enable showToolbarWithSidebar Needs Hide Toolbar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable showToolbarWithSidebar offers to turn it on too. FAQ Does the page move? Yes. The toolbar comes back in its usual place, so the page moves down under it, the same as with Hide toolbar off. Why doesn't it show when the sidebar slides out at the edge of the window? That sidebar floats over the page and goes away on its own, so the toolbar stays hidden. It shows once the sidebar is open beside the page. Does it work with tabs at the top? There's no sidebar with tabs at the top, so the toolbar stays hidden. Use Show Toolbar with Tabs at the Top to keep it there, or Show Toolbar on Hover.

title: Show Toolbar with Tabs at the Top
text: With Hide Toolbar on, put your tabs at the top and the toolbar stays, so the address bar is always there. Move your tabs back to the sidebar and it hides again. Tabs at the top Tabs in the sidebar :---::---: _Screenshot coming soon._ _Screenshot coming soon._ Why use it Hiding the toolbar suits the sidebar, where your tabs and the sidebar's own controls are a click away. With tabs at the top there's nothing else to type a URL into, so a hidden toolbar gets in the way. - Handy if you switch to tabs at the top now and then and want Dia to work as usual there. - The other Showing the Toolbar options still work in the sidebar. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Hide Toolbar and, under Showing the Toolbar, switch on Show Toolbar with Tabs at the Top. Or run: sh diatweaks enable showToolbarWithTopTabs Needs Hide Toolbar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable showToolbarWithTopTabs offers to turn it on too. FAQ Does the page move? With tabs at the top the toolbar sits in its usual place, the same as with Hide Toolbar off. Switching layouts moves the page the way Dia always does. Does it count a hidden sidebar as tabs at the top? No. A hidden or auto-hiding sidebar is still the sidebar layout, so the toolbar stays hidden there.

title: Toggle toolbar visibility
text: Press a keyboard shortcut to hide or show the toolbar, as Hide Toolbar does. It's ⌃D unless you set another. Why use it A shortcut is the quickest way to flip between a clean page and the full toolbar, and it doesn't depend on where the pointer is. - Use it if you like to hide the toolbar for reading and bring it back for a moment. - It works even when Hide Toolbar is off, so one key switches the whole feature. - Change the shortcut if ⌃D clashes with forward delete in text fields. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Hide Toolbar and, under Showing the Toolbar, switch on Toggle toolbar visibility. Or run: sh diatweaks enable toggleToolbarVisibility Change the shortcut Under the switch, click Shortcut and press the keys you want. It needs ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥, unless it's a function key. Press Delete to clear it, or Escape to keep the one you had. Needs Hide Toolbar. Settings lists this switch on that tweak's page. Once it's on, the shortcut works whether the toolbar is hidden or showing. FAQ Does ⌃D still delete forward in text fields? Yes, and it hides or shows the toolbar too. Set another shortcut if that gets in the way.

title: Show Toast When Copying URL
text: With Hide Toolbar on, ⇧⌘C or ⌥⇧⌘C shows a small Copied message at the top of the page, and the toolbar stays hidden. Why use it With the toolbar hidden you don't see Dia confirm a copied URL. A small toast tells you it worked without bringing the toolbar back. - Use it if you copy links often and want confirmation but a toolbar that stays hidden. - Dia 1.56 and later show their own message, so this only matters on older versions. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Hide Toolbar and, under Copying the URL, switch on Show Toast When Copying URL. Or run: sh diatweaks enable copyURLToast Needs Hide Toolbar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable copyURLToast offers to turn it on too. Works with Show Toolbar When Copying URL. With both on, the toolbar shows instead. FAQ Why can't I turn it on? From Dia 1.56, Dia shows its own Copied message at the top of the page while the toolbar is hidden, so this switch stays off.

title: Show Toolbar When Copying URL
text: With Hide Toolbar on, ⇧⌘C or ⌥⇧⌘C shows the toolbar for a moment, so you see Dia's Copied message in the address field. Then it hides again. Why use it With the toolbar hidden you don't see Dia confirm a copied URL. This shows the toolbar briefly so you get Dia's own message in the address field. - Use it if you want to see the real message, or the address you just copied. - Dia 1.56 and later show their own message, so this only matters on older versions. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Hide Toolbar and, under Copying the URL, switch on Show Toolbar When Copying URL. Or run: sh diatweaks enable peekToolbarOnCopy Needs Hide Toolbar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable peekToolbarOnCopy offers to turn it on too. Works with Show Toast When Copying URL. With both on, this one wins and the toast stays off. FAQ Why can't I turn it on? From Dia 1.56, Dia shows its own Copied message at the top of the page while the toolbar is hidden, so this switch stays off.

title: Show Loading Progress
text: With Hide Toolbar on, shows Dia's loading glow along the top of the page while it loads, where the hidden toolbar would have shown it. Why use it With the toolbar hidden you lose Dia's sign that a page is still loading. The glow gives it back along the top edge. - If you hide the toolbar, leave this on so slow pages don't look stuck. - Pick a color that suits your theme, or turn it off if you find the glow distracting. Turn it on or off It's on by default: turn on Hide Toolbar and it shows. To turn it off or back on, open Dia → Settings → Patches → Hide Toolbar and, under While It's Hidden, use Show Loading Progress. Or run: sh diatweaks enable showLoadingProgress Color Pick a color under the switch. Match Dia uses the colors Dia gives its own loading glow in each window. Accent Color follows the accent color in System Settings, and there are fixed choices: Blue, Purple, Pink, Orange, Green, Graphite and Jace, a brown. Needs Hide Toolbar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable showLoadingProgress offers to turn it on too.

title: Hide Site Color in Tab Bar
text: With tabs at the top and Hide Toolbar on, the selected tab keeps the page color and its normal title instead of the site's color. As the toolbar fades in on hover, the tab takes the site's color again, so the two still run into each other. Why use it Dia tints the selected tab with the site's color so it joins the toolbar below. With the toolbar hidden, that tint joins nothing and looks like a stray colored block. - Use it if you hide the toolbar and have tabs at the top. - Skip it if you like the site color in the tab bar. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Hide Toolbar and, under While It's Hidden, switch on Hide Site Color in Tab Bar. Or run: sh diatweaks enable plainSelectedTab Needs Hide Toolbar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable plainSelectedTab offers to turn it on too. FAQ Why does nothing change with tabs in the sidebar? Dia only fills the selected tab with the site's color when tabs are at the top.

title: Always Show Address Field
text: The address field keeps its background and its bookmark, split view and site buttons, as if you were pointing at it. You can see where the field is and reach the buttons without hovering first. Tabs in the sidebar Tabs at the top :---::---: Why use it Dia hides the field's frame and buttons until you point at it, so the toolbar can look empty and the buttons are easy to miss. - Handy if you use the bookmark, split view or site buttons often. - Skip it if you prefer the quieter toolbar. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Always Show Address Field. Or run: sh diatweaks enable showAddressField Works with Hide Toolbar. The field only shows while the toolbar does. FAQ Does it show the full address? That's Dia's own setting, and this tweak leaves it as it is.

title: Hide Sidebar Button
text: Hides the sidebar button at the top left of the toolbar. Tabs in the sidebar Tabs at the top :---::---: Why use it If you open and close the sidebar with the keyboard or never close it, the button is clutter. Removing it gives the toolbar a quieter corner. - Handy if you already use Dia's sidebar shortcut. - Skip it if you click the button to open the sidebar. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Sidebar Button. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideSidebarButton Works with While Hide Toolbar is on, the button is hidden with the rest of the toolbar and this switch is greyed out in Settings. With Show Toolbar on Hover too, the button stays hidden when the toolbar shows, as long as this tweak is on.

title: Don’t Open Downloads List
text: Stops the downloads list opening over the page each time a download starts. The downloads button still shows the download, and clicking it opens the list. Why use it Dia pops the downloads list over the page whenever a download starts, which covers what you're reading. - Handy if you download a lot, or start downloads from pages you want to keep looking at. - You still see progress on the button and can open the list when you want. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Don’t Open Downloads List. Or run: sh diatweaks enable quietDownloads FAQ Does it work with tabs at the top? Yes. The list stays closed there too, and the downloads button at the right of the tab bar opens it. Does it work with VoiceOver? Yes. Pressing the downloads button with VoiceOver or Full Keyboard Access opens the list as usual.

title: Hide Site Not Working Prompt
text: Stops the “not working correctly?” prompt that Dia shows under the ad blocker button after you reload a page a few times. Reloading still works, and the ad blocker stays as it was. Why use it After a few reloads Dia suggests turning off the ad blocker. If you reload often, or you know your sites work, the prompt keeps getting in the way. - Handy if you reload pages while developing or waiting on slow sites. - Skip it if the ad blocker sometimes breaks pages for you and you want the hint. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Site Not Working Prompt. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideReloadNudge FAQ How do I turn off the ad blocker for a site now? The same way as before the prompt: click the ad blocker button in the toolbar. Does it work with tabs at the top? Yes. The prompt stays hidden in both layouts.

title: Extensions Shortcut
text: Press a shortcut for a menu of your extensions at the top right of the page. Choosing one opens it as clicking its toolbar button would, pinned or not. Why use it Dia only reaches an extension through its toolbar button, and unpinned ones are buried. This lists them all from one key. - Handy if you use extensions often, or hide the toolbar. - Useful if you rely on the keyboard more than the mouse. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Extensions Shortcut. Or run: sh diatweaks enable extensionsShortcut Change the shortcut It's ⇧⌘X to begin with. Under the switch, click Shortcut and press the keys you want. It needs ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥, unless it's a function key. Press Delete to clear it, or Escape to keep the one you had. FAQ Which extensions does it list? Every extension that's on and has a toolbar button, whether or not it's pinned.

title: Profile Emoji
text: Gives each profile an emoji, which takes the place of its dot in the profile switcher. Tabs in the sidebar Tabs at the top :---::---: Why use it Profiles are told apart only by small colored dots, which look alike when you have several. - Handy if you switch between work, personal and other profiles often. - An emoji is faster to spot than a dot color. Turn it on It's on by default. To check, open Dia → Settings → Patches and look for Profile Emoji. Or run: sh diatweaks enable profileEmoji Then open Dia → Settings → Profiles, choose a profile, and click the Emoji field under Theme Color to pick one. Clear the field to get the dot back. FAQ Does it work with tabs at the top? Yes. Hover the profile's name beside the pinned tabs and the emoji show where the dots would.

title: Switch Profiles with ⌘1–9
text: Press ⌘ and a number to switch to that profile, in the order of the dots at the bottom of the sidebar, like Arc's spaces. Dia's shortcuts for the sidebar's items move to ⌃ and a number, so nothing is lost. Why use it Dia has no ready shortcut for jumping to a profile. This gives you one, like Arc's spaces. - Handy if you keep work and personal profiles and switch often. - The cost is that the sidebar items move to ⌃ and a number. Skip it if you rely on ⌘1–9 for those. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Switch Profiles with ⌘1–9. Or run: sh diatweaks enable profileShortcuts FAQ Why doesn't Dia's own Shortcuts setting do this? Dia lets you set ⌘1 for a profile there, but a page takes ⌘ and a number before Dia's menu sees it, and the sidebar's items already have it. This swaps the two and catches the keys before the page does. What does ⌘9 do? It goes to your last profile, as ⌃9 went to the last sidebar item. My keyboard needs Shift for numbers. Which keys do I press? On AZERTY and other layouts where the number row types symbols, press ⌘⇧ and the number key. That is how macOS itself matches ⌘1 on those layouts.

title: Translucent Sidebar
text: Lets the page show through the sidebar when it floats over it, with the sidebar hidden, instead of the theme color covering it. Why use it The floating sidebar covers part of the page with a solid color. With this it lets the page show through, which looks lighter and keeps context. - Handy if you use the hidden, floating sidebar and like a glassy look. - Skip it if you find text hard to read over busy pages. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Translucent Sidebar. Or run: sh diatweaks enable translucentSidebar FAQ Can I change the material? Yes. Turn on Window Material and pick one there. With Window material off, it uses the same material as the window's background.

title: Sidebar Grain
text: Adds a fine texture behind your tabs, like paper or fabric. It sits behind the sidebar, and behind the tab bar when your tabs are at the top. Tabs in the sidebar Tabs at the top :---::---: Why use it Dia's sidebar and tab bar are smooth. A little texture gives them some feel, and it stays behind your tabs, so they look and work the same. - Handy if you want the window to feel less flat. - Skip it if you like Dia's clean, smooth look. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Sidebar Grain. Or run: sh diatweaks enable sidebarGrain Options The options sit under the switch in Settings, with a small preview. - Texture: Grain, Sand, Tweed, Denim, Matte or Fine. The default is Sand. - Grain: how strong the texture is, from 0% to 100%. The default is 50%. - Softness: how much the texture is blurred, from 0% to 100%. The default is 0%. - Scale: how large the texture is, from 50% to 300%. The default is 100%. - Reset puts grain, softness and scale back to their defaults. You can also change them without opening Settings: right-click an empty part of the sidebar and choose Edit Sidebar Grain…. With tabs at the top, right-click an empty part of the tab bar. Each profile its own grain In Edit Sidebar Grain…, set Apply to to This Profile to give the profile you're in its own texture, grain, softness and scale, or untick Show grain in this profile to turn it off there. Anything you don't change follows the settings for all profiles. Reset clears that profile's own settings. Settings always edits the settings for all profiles. FAQ Does it work with tabs at the top? Yes. The texture goes behind the tab bar instead of the sidebar. Can each profile have a different grain? Yes. Right-click the sidebar, choose Edit Sidebar Grain… and set Apply to to This Profile. Each window shows the grain of the profile it's on, and switches with it. Does it get in the way of clicking? No. Clicks pass straight through it to your tabs. Why does the texture fade when I switch to another app? It follows the window. When the window isn't the active one, the texture hides, like the rest of Dia's window styling. Why doesn't "Edit Sidebar Grain…" show up on my tabs? It only appears when you right-click empty space. Right-clicking a tab gives you the tab's own menu.

title: Compact Sidebar Header
text: Moves the pinned tabs up into the empty space under the window buttons, and puts the window buttons where Dia puts them with tabs at the top. It only changes the sidebar, so it does nothing with tabs at the top. Why use it The sidebar header leaves an empty band beside the window buttons. Moving the pinned tabs up into it frees room for the tab list. - Handy if you have a short screen or lots of tabs. - It only affects tabs in the sidebar. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Compact Sidebar Header. Or run: sh diatweaks enable compactSidebarHeader FAQ Does it change the sidebar that floats over the page? Yes, its header is trimmed too, so the pinned tabs and window buttons move up a little. The buttons only go to the top-tabs spot when they're already near the window's corner, which they aren't in the floating sidebar.

title: Compact Tab Rows
text: Makes the sidebar's tabs and folders as short as they were before Dia 1.57, 37 points a row instead of 41, so more tabs fit. It only changes the sidebar, so it does nothing with tabs at the top. _Screenshot coming soon._ Why use it Dia 1.57 made every row in the sidebar 4 points taller. With a long list that adds up: 20 tabs take 80 points more than before. - Handy if you keep lots of tabs or folders open. - On a Dia whose rows are already 37 points, it does nothing. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and, under Sidebar & Tab Bar, switch on Compact Tab Rows. Or run: sh diatweaks enable compactTabRows FAQ What changes? Each tab, folder and the New Tab row is 4 points shorter, and the tab's highlight is 34 points tall instead of 38. Open folders shrink by their header and every row inside them. Icons, titles and spacing between rows stay as they are.

title: Narrower Sidebar
text: Lets the sidebar shrink to 164 points, as narrow as Arc's, instead of stopping at Dia's 190. Drag the sidebar's edge to make it narrower. _Screenshot coming soon._ Why use it Dia won't let the sidebar get narrower than 190 points. On a small screen that's a lot of width for tab titles you can read at a glance. - Handy on a laptop screen, or with short tab titles. - Pinned tabs reflow to fit the narrower width. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and, under Sidebar & Tab Bar, switch on Narrower Sidebar. Or run: sh diatweaks enable narrowerSidebar FAQ What happens when I turn it off? The sidebar goes back to stopping at 190 points the next time you resize it. Why is it greyed out? Dia has no setting for the narrowest width, so this changes the one instruction that sets it. If a Dia update changes that code, the switch stays off until DiaTweaks is updated, rather than change something else.

title: Hide Pinned Tab Border
text: Removes the colored border around the selected pinned tab. The tab keeps its tint, so you can still tell which one is selected. Tabs in the sidebar Tabs at the top :---::---: Why use it The colored border on the selected pinned tab can look heavy next to the tint. - Handy if you want a quieter, flatter look. - Skip it if you rely on the border to spot the selected tab. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Pinned Tab Border. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hidePinnedTabBorder FAQ Does it work with tabs at the top? Yes.

title: Hide Pinned Tab Card
text: Stops the card with a pinned tab's title, address and buttons from popping up when you point at the tab. Click the tab as usual; right-click it for the same actions. Why use it The card pops up whenever you point at a pinned tab, even when you're just passing over it. - Handy if you move through pinned tabs often and find the card distracting. - Skip it if you use the card's buttons often. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Pinned Tab Card. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hidePinnedTabCard FAQ Where did Reset, Bookmark and Split go? They're in the pinned tab's right-click menu too.

title: Hide Vertical Tab Glow
text: Removes the selected sidebar tab's glow and glass highlights, and gives its border one even color. The title, favicon and what the tab does stay the same. Tabs at the top keep Dia's own look. Why use it The glow and fading edge can make the selected tab stand out more than you want. This makes it flatter and keeps a clear outline. - Handy if you want a quieter sidebar. - Skip it if you like the glow to spot the selected tab. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Vertical Tab Glow. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideVerticalTabGlow It only works with tabs in the sidebar. FAQ What happens to the selected tab's border? It keeps its shape. The border that fades from one color to another becomes a single, even color from Dia's own palette, so it still follows light and dark mode. Does it work with tabs at the top? No. Tabs at the top keep Dia's original styling. What happens when I turn it off? Dia's shadow, border colors and glass highlights come back.

title: Collapse Pinned Tabs
text: Adds a Pinned line above your pinned tabs and folders in the sidebar. Click it to fold them away, like in Arc, and click again to bring them back. For now it only works with tabs in the sidebar. Why use it With a lot of pinned tabs and folders, the tabs you have open today end up far down the sidebar, and you scroll past the pinned ones to reach them. Folded, your favorites stay at the top and today's tabs sit right below. Skip it if you'd rather see your pinned tabs all the time. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Collapse Pinned Tabs. Or run: sh diatweaks enable collapsePinned Use it - Click anywhere on the Pinned line to fold or unfold. The chevron points down while they're showing and right while they're folded. - Each profile remembers which way you left it, across windows and after you quit Dia. - Drag tabs as usual. To pin one while they're folded, hold it over the Pinned line for a moment and they unfold. A tab dropped right on the folded line goes back where it was, so nothing gets pinned out of sight. FAQ Does it work with tabs at the top? No. With tabs at the top, pinned tabs are in the tab bar and nothing changes there. The line comes back when you switch to the sidebar. Where are my favorites? Still at the top. Only the pinned tabs and folders below them fold. I opened a pinned tab and I can't see it in the sidebar. While they're folded, pinned tabs stay hidden, even the one you're on. Unfold to see it.

title: Hide Group Background
text: Leaves an open tab group without the grey box Dia draws behind it, so groups look like Arc's folders. A group you've given a color keeps it. Why use it The grey box behind a tab group adds visual weight, especially with several groups open. - Handy if you want groups to look like Arc's folders. - Colored groups keep their color, so you still tell them apart. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Group Background. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideTabGroupBackground FAQ Does it change groups I picked a color for? No. Only the grey a group gets when it has no color of its own goes.

title: Hide Recent Tabs Button
text: Hides the recent tabs button: the small arrow next to Chats at the bottom of the sidebar, or its button in the tab bar when tabs are at the top. Tabs in the sidebar Tabs at the top :---::---: Why use it If you never use the recent tabs list, its button is clutter next to Chats. - Handy if you want a quieter bottom of the sidebar or tab bar. - Skip it if you reopen recent tabs from there. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Recent Tabs Button. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideRecentTabsButton

title: Show Repo on Pull Requests
text: In a GitHub live folder, shows each pull request's repository, number and state under its title, instead of its author. The review status moves to a line of its own. Why use it In Created by Me the author is always you, so the line under each title tells you nothing. The repository and number tell pull requests apart, and the review status no longer gets cut off. - Before: octocat • Changes Requested - After: hello-world 42 · Open, with Changes Requested on the line below Skip it if you'd rather see who opened each pull request. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Show Repo on Pull Requests. Or run: sh diatweaks enable pullRequestRepo FAQ Does it work with tabs at the top? Yes, but the review status stays on the repository line instead of getting its own, so it can be cut off. Only the sidebar's list can make a row taller. What about merged pull requests? A status that only repeats the state, like Merged ✓, replaces the state on the repository line. It doesn't get a line of its own. Does it show the owner too? No, just the repository's name, like hello-world. Does it work on anything but pull requests? No. It only changes GitHub pull requests in live folders.

title: Keep Folders Open
text: Keeps a folder open when it empties by itself, so new items show up. A folder you fold away yourself stays folded. Why use it Some folders fill themselves, like Dia's live folders of GitHub pull requests. When the last item goes, Dia folds the folder, and it stays folded when new items arrive. You can miss them. This opens the folder again. - Handy if you use live folders and want to see new items. - Skip it if you like Dia folding empty folders. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Keep Folders Open. Or run: sh diatweaks enable keepFoldersOpen It works with tabs in the sidebar and at the top. FAQ Does it open a folder I folded myself? No. If you click a folder to fold it, it stays folded. Only folders that Dia folds on its own are opened again. Does it work with tabs at the top? Yes. A folder in the tab bar that Dia folds on its own is opened again, and one you fold yourself stays folded. Why does a normal folder still go away? A folder you made yourself disappears when its last tab closes. This is for live folders, which stay and fill up again.

title: Open Sidebar Instantly
text: Opens the hidden sidebar the moment you move the pointer to the left edge of the window, with none of Dia's short wait. Why use it With the sidebar hidden, Dia waits about a tenth of a second after the pointer reaches the edge before it opens the sidebar. It's short, but it adds up if you reach for the sidebar a lot. With this on, the sidebar starts opening straight away, like the desktop switcher in Mission Control. Skip it if you like the small pause, which keeps the sidebar from opening when the pointer only grazes the edge. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Open Sidebar Instantly. Or run: sh diatweaks enable openSidebarInstantly Hide the sidebar with ⌘S, or from the sidebar button, then move the pointer to the left edge. FAQ Does it change the animation or how the sidebar closes? No. Dia still slides the sidebar in and still closes it when the pointer leaves, after the same wait as before. Only the wait before it opens is gone. Does it work with tabs at the top? There's no sidebar to open, so nothing changes there, but one thing does. Dia uses the same wait for a hidden tab bar at the top, so that shows sooner too when you move the pointer to the top edge. Will it keep working after Dia updates? It may need an update after some Dia releases. The wait is a number inside Dia's code, with no setting for it, so this tweak changes that one instruction while Dia runs and puts it back when you turn the tweak off. Nothing on disk changes. It finds the spot by the code around it. After a Dia release that changes that code, it can't find the spot, shows as unavailable in Settings and does nothing, and it needs an update. It never changes anything it doesn't recognize.

title: Tidy Tabs
text: Groups your tabs by what they're for, like Arc's Tidy Tabs. A broom shows on the line above your tabs, beside Close All, and clicking it puts tabs about the same thing into groups that Dia names. Why use it If your sidebar fills up with tabs from a day of research, sorting them by hand is slow. The broom sorts them in one click, and ⌘Z undoes it if you don't like the result. It suits people who open many tabs and want them in named groups. It does nothing for a short list, since the broom only shows with more than 5 tabs below the line, and it needs Apple Intelligence on your Mac. Use it With tabs in the sidebar, point at the line above your tabs and click the broom. The line ripples while it works. Press ⌘Z right after to put the tabs back where they were. The broom shows when there are more than 5 tabs below the line. It leaves favorites, pinned tabs and tabs already in a group alone, and only groups tabs that clearly belong together. Needs - A Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) on macOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence turned on. Without it, the broom still shows, and pointing at it or clicking it says why it can't tidy. - Tabs in the sidebar. With tabs at the top there's no line for the broom. Turn on Apple Intelligence 1. Open System Settings and choose Apple Intelligence & Siri in the sidebar. 2. Switch on Apple Intelligence. 3. Leave your Mac connected to the internet and to power while it downloads the models. Until it's done, the broom says "Apple Intelligence is still downloading". If a setting stops Apple Intelligence from downloading at all, such as Siri and your Mac using different languages, the broom says which one to change instead. If the switch isn't there or can't be turned on: - Set your Mac's language and Siri's language to the same supported language, such as English. Change them in System Settings → General → Language & Region and in Apple Intelligence & Siri. - Make room: Apple Intelligence needs up to 14 GB free. - Apple Intelligence isn't available in every country or region, or when your Mac starts up from an external drive. Apple's own guide is Get started with Apple Intelligence on your Mac. How the broom finds the setting is in Discoveries: Apple Intelligence. Turn it on It's off by default. Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Tidy Tabs. Or run: sh diatweaks enable tidyTabs FAQ Does it send my tabs anywhere? No. It sends each tab's title and address, without the part after ?, to Apple's model on your Mac. Dia names the groups itself, as it does for any group. Why are the same tabs always grouped the same way? The model is asked for its single most likely answer each time, so the same tabs give the same groups. Thanks @baginski11 (129).

title: Unload Tabs
text: Adds Unload Tab to a tab's right-click menu. It frees the memory the page uses but keeps the tab where it is, and the page loads again when you open it. Why use it Tabs you've left open for later keep their pages in memory. Unload Tab frees that memory without closing the tab or losing its place in the sidebar. Handy when your Mac is slow or low on memory and you have heavy pages, like web apps or video sites, that you want to keep but aren't using. Skip it for pages with unsaved work, since they reload from scratch. Use it Right-click a tab and choose Unload Tab. If it's the tab you're on, you go back to the tab you were on before, then it unloads. An open pinned tab goes back to its pinned page, like the minus button. The page reloads from scratch when you open the tab again, so anything you'd typed into it that the site didn't save is gone. Turn it on It's off by default. Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Unload Tabs. Or run: sh diatweaks enable unloadTab FAQ Why is Unload Tab greyed out? The page is on screen somewhere Dia can't leave, such as another window, or it's the only tab in the window, so there's nowhere to go back to. Why isn't Unload Tab in the menu? It only shows for a tab whose page has loaded, isn't unloaded already, and isn't split. It also stays out when another loaded tab has the same address, so it never unloads the wrong one. Why does an unloaded tab look the same? Dia doesn't mark the tabs it unloads itself, or hasn't loaded yet, so an unloaded tab looks like any other. Unload Tab leaves its menu until you open the tab again. Dia keeps some pages loaded, such as one playing audio.

title: Group Tabs by Domain
text: Puts tabs from the same site into a group named after it, like YouTube or Wikipedia. It groups once, each time you choose it. Why use it Handy when a window has filled up with tabs from a few sites, like a research session or a long day of links. One command tidies them into groups you can fold away, without Dia's AI picking the names. Use Tidy Tabs instead if you'd rather group by topic than by site. Use it Right-click a tab and choose Group Tabs by Domain, choose Tabs → Group Tabs by Domain, or press ⌃⇧G. It groups the tabs in the front window. Press ⌘Z right after to put them back where they were. The same menus have: - Group Selected Tabs by Domain: groups only the tabs you've selected, with ⌘-click or ⇧-click. - Expand All Tab Groups and Collapse All Tab Groups: open or close every group in the front window. - Ungroup This Domain: takes apart the current tab's site group. The tabs stay open. - Ungroup All Domains: takes apart every site group in the front window. Groups you named yourself stay. ⌘Z right after either ungroup puts the groups back. Shortcut Open Dia → Settings → Patches, click the chevron next to Group Tabs by Domain, and set Shortcut. If the keys already belong to a Dia menu item or another tweak, it says so. Merge Subdomains Off, docs.example.com and example.com get their own groups. Turn on Merge Subdomains to put them in one. Sites where each subdomain belongs to someone else, like github.io, stay apart. Turn it off It's on by default. To take it out of both menus, open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch off Group Tabs by Domain. Or run: sh diatweaks disable groupTabsByDomain FAQ Does it read my pages? No. It only looks at each tab's address. Which tabs does it leave alone? Pinned tabs, tabs already in a group, new tab pages, files and Dia's own pages. A site needs at least two tabs to get a group. What if I already have a group for a site? If a group's name is the site, like GitHub or github.com, that site's tabs join it instead of making a new group. Are www.example.com and example.com the same site? Yes, it ignores www.. Other subdomains, like docs.example.com, get their own group unless Merge Subdomains is on. Why is a group named after the address? When two sites would get the same name, like apple.com and apple.org, each keeps its address so the groups stay apart. Addresses like localhost keep theirs too.

title: Merge Subdomains
text: With Group Tabs by Domain, puts tabs from the same site in one group even when they're on different subdomains. gist.github.com joins github.com, and developer.apple.com joins apple.com. Why use it Some sites spread one product over several subdomains, like mail.google.com and docs.google.com, or old.reddit.com and www.reddit.com. Off, each subdomain gets its own group, which can leave you with a handful of small groups for one site. Turn this on if you think of those as one site. Leave it off if you want docs.example.com kept apart from example.com. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Group Tabs by Domain and, under Options, switch on Merge Subdomains. Or run: sh diatweaks enable groupTabsMergeSubdomains Needs Group Tabs by Domain. Settings greys out this switch until that's on. FAQ How does it know what the site is? It keeps the last two parts of the address, so news.example.com becomes example.com. Under a two-letter country ending with a common second part, like .co.uk or .com.au, it keeps three, so news.bbc.co.uk becomes bbc.co.uk. It's a short rule rather than the full list browsers use, so the odd site may group differently from what you expect. Why aren't my github.io sites merged? On sites like github.io, vercel.app, netlify.app, pages.dev and blogspot.com, each subdomain belongs to someone else, so each one stays its own site. What about addresses like localhost or 192.168.1.10? They're left as they are.

title: Close Tabs from Tab Switcher
text: Press W or ⌘W while the tab switcher is open to close the highlighted tab. The switcher stays open on the next tab, so you can keep closing or switching. Why use it Dia's tab switcher lets you jump between tabs, but not clear out the ones you don't need. With this, you can close tabs as you cycle past them and never leave the keyboard. Handy when you're tidying up a pile of tabs. It's on by default, so turn it off only if pressing W in the switcher by accident bothers you. Use it Hold ⌃ and press ⇥ to open the tab switcher, move to a tab, then press W or ⌘W while you still hold ⌃. Let go of ⌃ to switch to the highlighted tab, as usual. Turn it off It's on by default. Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch off Close Tabs from Tab Switcher. Or run: sh diatweaks disable closeFromTabSwitcher FAQ Why does the switcher flicker after I close a tab? Dia's switcher doesn't update while it's open, so it closes and opens again without the tab, back on the same spot.

title: Save Page As
text: Adds Save Page As… to the File menu, above Print, with a shortcut. It saves the page you're on, as Chrome does, which Dia only offers in the page's right-click menu. Why use it Dia only offers Save Page As… in a page's right-click menu, so there's no menu item or shortcut for it. This adds one to the File menu, like Chrome. Use it when you want to keep a copy of a page, like an article or receipt, as a file on your Mac. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Save Page As. Or run: sh diatweaks enable savePageAs Change the shortcut It's ⌥⌘S to begin with, because ⌘S shows and hides the sidebar. Under the switch, click Shortcut and press the keys you want. It needs ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥, unless it's a function key. Press Delete to clear it, or Escape to keep the one you had.

title: Undo Closing a Tab
text: Closed a tab by mistake? Press ⌘Z straight away and it comes back, like History › Reopen Closed Tab (⇧⌘T). You can set another shortcut on its Settings page. It only works right after closing: once you type or click, ⌘Z goes back to undoing whatever you're doing. Why use it It's easy to close the wrong tab, and ⇧⌘T is a long reach. This lets ⌘Z, which you already press to undo, bring the tab back. Handy if you undo by habit. It only takes the shortcut right after a tab closes, so it doesn't get in the way of undo in text fields. If you'd rather keep ⇧⌘T, leave it off. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Undo Closing a Tab. Or run: sh diatweaks enable undoCloseTab FAQ Does it get in the way of ⌘Z in text fields? No. ⌘Z only reopens a tab if closing it was the last thing you did. Typing, clicking or any other key in between hands ⌘Z back to the page or field you're in. What about undoing Tidy Tabs? ⌘Z undoes whichever happened last. Tidy your tabs and then close one, and ⌘Z reopens the tab; tidy after closing, and ⌘Z undoes the tidy. Does it work with tabs at the top? Yes, in both layouts.

title: Pin Tab Shortcut
text: Press ⌘D to move the tab you're on to the bottom of your pinned tabs, like in Arc. Press it on a pinned tab to unpin it. Why use it Dia's own Pin/Unpin Tab shortcut adds the tab to your favorites at the top. Putting a tab with your pinned tabs, above the line, is only in a tab's right-click menu as Pin as Tab. This puts it on a key. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Pin Tab Shortcut. Or run: sh diatweaks enable pinTabShortcut Change the shortcut It's ⌘D to begin with. Under the switch, click Shortcut and press the keys you want. It needs ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥, unless it's a function key. Press Delete to clear it, or Escape to keep the one you had. FAQ What happened to Bookmark This Page? With this on, ⌘D pins instead. It still bookmarks when there's nothing to pin: on a favorite, on a tab inside a pinned folder, or in a window without tabs. Set another shortcut to keep ⌘D for bookmarks. Where does an unpinned tab go? Where Dia puts new tabs, the same as choosing Unpin from its right-click menu. I pinned a tab and it disappeared. With Collapse Pinned Tabs folded, a tab you pin joins the folded pinned tabs. Unfold them to see it.

title: Open New Tabs Next to Current
text: A new tab opens right after the tab you're on, not at the end of the list, like in Arc and Chrome. Close it and you go back to the tab you came from. Why use it Dia puts a new tab at the bottom of your tabs, so a tab you open to look something up ends up far from the one you were reading. With this on, it sits next to it, and closing it brings you straight back. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Open New Tabs Next to Current. Or run: sh diatweaks enable newTabNextToCurrent Where the new tab goes - On a tab in the list: right after it. - On a favorite or a pinned tab: at the top of the tabs below the line, as in Arc. - On a tab in a folder: right after the folder. - With tabs at the top: right after the tab you're on, the same way. This covers File → New Tab, its shortcut whatever you've set it to, and the New Tab button in the sidebar. A tab you open from a link isn't moved. Closing the new tab takes you back to the tab you opened it from, unless you've gone to another tab since. Going back to that tab and then to the new one keeps it. Works with Open New Tabs in Command Bar. The bar shows over the tab you were on, and the new tab waits next to it. Press Escape and it's gone. FAQ Pressing the shortcut on a New Tab page doesn't open another. That's how Dia works: on a new tab page, New Tab just brings you back to it. The new tab flickers in the sidebar for a moment. Dia can only put a new tab at the end, so the tweak makes it, then moves it. Moving takes a fraction of a second.

title: Mouse Back and Forward Buttons
text: Makes your mouse's side buttons go back and forward in Dia, even when a site or your mouse driver stops Dia seeing them. With split tabs, it goes back or forward in the page under the pointer. Why use it Some mice, or their drivers, send back and forward as swipes instead of ordinary side-button clicks, and Dia ignores those. This catches them and moves through the page's history. - Handy if your mouse's side buttons do nothing in Dia. - Skip it if they already work for you. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Mouse Back and Forward Buttons. Or run: sh diatweaks enable mouseBackForward What it handles - The side buttons themselves (buttons 4 and 5, which macOS numbers 3 and 4). It goes back or forward when you let go. - A back or forward swipe that a driver such as SteerMouse sends with no window attached. It works out the window from where the pointer is, and does one step per swipe. Two-finger trackpad swipes and vertical swipes are left alone. Which page it moves - Over a page, that page. - Over the sidebar or toolbar, the page you're on. - With split tabs, the page under the pointer. If the page has nowhere to go, nothing happens. FAQ Does it work with tabs at the top? Yes, in both layouts. Does it change the trackpad? No. Two-finger swipes on a trackpad work as Dia always had them.

title: Hide Sleeping Tabs
text: Leaves tabs with nothing loaded, like a pinned tab you closed, out of the tab switcher (⌃⇥), instead of showing them as empty pictures. The switcher fits the tabs left, and cycling skips the others. Why use it The tab switcher shows a tab with nothing loaded, like a pinned tab you closed, as an empty picture, and cycling lands on it. This leaves those tabs out so every stop has a page to show. Handy if you pin many tabs. You can still reach a hidden tab from the sidebar. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Sleeping Tabs. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideSleepingTabs FAQ Can I still get to a pinned tab I closed? Yes. Click it in the sidebar, or turn this off.

title: Close Button on Pinned Tabs
text: Shows a close button when you point at a pinned tab outside a folder, like Dia already does for tabs in a pinned folder. Why use it Dia hides the close button on pinned tabs that aren't in a folder. This shows it when you point at the tab. - Handy if you pin tabs and want to close them with a click. - Skip it if you like pinned tabs that can't be closed by accident. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Close Button on Pinned Tabs. Or run: sh diatweaks enable pinnedTabCloseButton It's off by default. It works with tabs in the sidebar and at the top. Works with Minus Button on Open Pinned Tabs swaps the ✕ for a – on pinned tabs with a page open, so you can close the page and keep the tab. FAQ What does the button do? It closes the pinned tab and removes it, like the button on tabs in a pinned folder. Does it change pinned tabs in a folder? No. Dia already shows the button there.

title: Minus Button on Open Pinned Tabs
text: Shows a – button instead of ✕ on pinned tabs with a page open, in or out of a folder, like Arc. It closes the page and keeps the tab pinned. Why use it The ✕ on a pinned tab removes it. Often you only want to close the page and keep the tab where it is. Dia has a – for that, but only under a folded folder. This gives it to every open pinned tab. - Handy if you pin tabs you come back to. - Skip it if you'd rather have ✕ everywhere. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Close Button on Pinned Tabs and switch on Minus Button on Open Pinned Tabs. Or run: sh diatweaks enable pinnedTabMinusButton It's off by default. It works with tabs in the sidebar and at the top. Needs Close Button on Pinned Tabs. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable pinnedTabMinusButton offers to turn it on too. FAQ What if the pinned tab has no page open? It still shows ✕, and ✕ removes the tab, because there's no page to close. Does it change tabs that already have a –? No. Tabs under a folded folder and split tabs keep what Dia gives them.

title: Compact Command Bar
text: If your account has no chat usage, the command bar's Add tabs or files and dictation buttons only say they need it. This hides them and moves Go up beside what you type, so the bar fits on one line: in the bar from ⌘L, on the new tab page, and in Command bar. Why use it Without chat usage, Add tabs or files and the dictation button can't be used, but they still take up room and make the bar two lines tall. This hides them so the bar is one line. If your account has no chat usage, you lose nothing. If you have chat usage, the bar stays as it is unless you also turn on Compact with Chat Usage Too. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Compact Command Bar. Or run: sh diatweaks enable compactCommandBar Options On the same page, once it's on: - Compact with Chat Usage Too compacts the bar even when you have chat usage. FAQ Why don't I see a difference? With chat usage, those buttons work, so the bar keeps them. To compact it anyway, turn on Compact with Chat Usage Too under its Options. That hides Add tabs or files and dictation even though you could use them.

title: Compact with Chat Usage Too
text: Compacts the command bar like Compact Command Bar does, even when your account has chat usage. That hides Add tabs or files and dictation, so you can't use them from the command bar while it's on. Why use it If you have chat usage but never use Add tabs or files or dictation, this gives you the same one-line bar. You can't use those buttons from the command bar while it's on, so skip it if you attach tabs or files, or dictate, there. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Compact Command Bar and switch on Compact with Chat Usage Too. Or run: sh diatweaks enable compactCommandBarWithChat Needs Compact Command Bar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable compactCommandBarWithChat offers to turn it on too.

title: Open New Tabs in Command Bar
text: A new tab opens as Dia's command bar over the page you're on, like Arc, instead of as a new tab page. It's the same bar the new tab page has, so its suggestions, chats, @ and / all work as usual. Why use it A new tab page takes over the page you were reading. This opens the command bar over the page instead, so you can search or go somewhere and go back with Escape, like Arc. It suits people who open a new tab only to type an address or a question. If you like browsing from the new tab page, its shortcuts and tiles, leave it off. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Open New Tabs in Command Bar. Or run: sh diatweaks enable commandBar Use it Press your New Tab shortcut or click New Tab, then type. Press Return or click a suggestion to open it in a new tab. Press Escape or ⌘W, or click outside the bar, to go back to the page you were on. Pressing the shortcut again while the bar is open just puts you back in it. With Hide Toolbar on, ⌘L opens the same bar in the same place, filled in with the page's address, and what you pick opens in the tab you're on instead of a new one. When the toolbar is showing, ⌘L opens Dia's own bar under the address field as usual. Close a window's last tab and the window goes blank, with no new tab page and no bar. Your New Tab shortcut or the New Tab button opens the bar over the blank window without making another tab, and what you pick opens right there. With no page behind it, the bar doesn't blur or darken anything. Options On the same page, once it's on: Options - Position: Like Spotlight puts the bar centred across the screen, a little above the middle, kept inside the Dia window. Center of Window puts it in the middle of the window. Center of Page puts it in the middle of the page, so it moves over when the sidebar is open. - Space Above Bar sets how far down the bar sits. Blur - Blur Page Behind, on to begin with. It covers the page and moves with it when the sidebar slides, but leaves the sidebar alone. - Blur Radius sets how strong the blur is. - Blur Sidebar Too blurs the whole window behind the bar. Darken - Darken Page Behind, on to begin with, like the blur. - Darkness sets how dark it gets. Shadow - Shadow Behind Bar, on to begin with, puts a soft shadow around the bar so it stands out on a page of the same colour, even with Blur and Darken off. - Shadow Intensity sets how dark the shadow is. Interaction - Scroll Page Behind, on to begin with, lets you scroll the page under the bar while it's open, like Arc. Pointing at the page doesn't highlight anything, and clicking it only closes the bar. Typing - Remember What You Typed, off to begin with, so the bar comes back with what you typed before Escape. For the sliders, type a number into the box beside one, or press ↑ and ↓ to step it by 1, or by 10 with Shift. To go back to the defaults, set them to these: Option Default --- --- Space above the bar 30% Darkness 24% Blur radius 4 pt Blur the sidebar too Off Shadow intensity 30% FAQ Why does a New Tab show in the sidebar while the bar is open? The bar opens a real tab and waits there, so whatever you pick loads in it. Going back closes it. What about a new window? It opens with the bar over it, without blur or darkening. Going back closes the window. Why does a blank window still show a New Tab in the sidebar? Dia always keeps a tab in a window, so the blank window is that tab with its new tab page hidden. It closes as soon as you move to another tab. Why doesn't ⌘L show a New Tab in the sidebar? It edits the tab you're on, so there's no new tab to wait in. The bar is Dia's own ⌘L bar, moved out of the address field and laid out like the new tab page's.

title: Blur Page Behind
text: Blurs the page behind the command bar while it's open. Why use it A blurred page keeps your eyes on the command bar and hides text behind it that would compete with what you type. Turn it off if you want to read the page while you type, or if you find the blur slow on your Mac. Turn it off It's on by default. Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Open New Tabs in Command Bar and, under Blur, switch off Blur Page Behind. Or run: sh diatweaks disable commandBarBlur Options Under Blur on the command bar page, Blur Radius sets how strong the blur is (4 pt to begin with), and Blur Sidebar Too blurs the whole window behind the bar instead of only the page. Needs Command bar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable commandBarBlur offers to turn it on too. Works with Darken Page Behind. With both on, the page is blurred and darkened.

title: Darken Page Behind
text: Darkens the page behind the command bar while it's open. Why use it Dimming the page makes the command bar stand out, especially over a bright page. Turn it off if you want the page to keep its colors, or set Darkness low for a light dim. Turn it off It's on by default. Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Open New Tabs in Command Bar and, under Darken, switch off Darken Page Behind. Or run: sh diatweaks disable commandBarDarken Options Under Darken on the command bar page, Darkness sets how dark the page gets (24% to begin with). Needs Command bar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable commandBarDarken offers to turn it on too. Works with Blur Page Behind. With both on, the page is blurred and darkened.

title: Shadow Behind Bar
text: Adds a shadow behind the command bar, like Arc's, so it stands out when Blur Page Behind and Darken Page Behind are off. Why use it Without blur or darkening, the command bar can blend into a busy page. The shadow lifts it off the page and keeps the page itself untouched. Turn it off if you want a flat bar. Turn it off It's on by default. Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Open New Tabs in Command Bar and, under Shadow, switch off Shadow Behind Bar. Or run: sh diatweaks disable commandBarShadow Needs Command bar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable commandBarShadow offers to turn it on too. Works with Blur Page Behind and Darken Page Behind. The shadow shows with them too, but it matters most when both are off.

title: Scroll Page Behind
text: Lets you scroll the page behind the command bar while the bar is open, like in Arc. Why use it You can look further down the page while you type, without closing the bar. The pointer doesn't highlight links on the page while the bar is open. Clicking the page closes the bar and the click goes to the page. Turn it off if you want the page to stay put while the bar is open. Turn it off It's on by default. Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Open New Tabs in Command Bar and, under Interaction, switch off Scroll Page Behind. Or run: sh diatweaks disable commandBarInteractive Needs Command bar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable commandBarInteractive offers to turn it on too.

title: Remember What You Typed
text: Brings back what you typed in the command bar when you open it again after Escape, ⌘W or a click outside, like Arc. The text comes back selected, so you can carry on or type over it. Each window keeps its own text. Choosing a result starts the next bar empty, and so does emptying the bar before Escape. Why use it If you press Escape by accident, or leave the bar to check something on the page, you lose what you were typing. This brings it back, selected, when you open the bar again. Handy for long searches and questions. Leave it off if you'd rather start with an empty bar every time. Turn it on It's off by default. Open Dia → Settings → Patches → Open New Tabs in Command Bar and, under Typing, switch on Remember What You Typed. Or run: sh diatweaks enable commandBarKeepText Needs Command bar. Settings greys out this switch until that's on, and diatweaks enable commandBarKeepText offers to turn it on too.

title: Hide History Suggestions
text: Leaves pages you've visited and searches you've made before out of the suggestions in the address field and the command bar. Searching, Chat, search suggestions and switching to open tabs still show. Why use it Old pages and searches in the suggestion list can bury what you're looking for, and show things you'd rather not see when someone is looking at your screen. Handy if you want suggestions to be only searches and open tabs. You lose the shortcut of typing a few letters to reach a page you've visited before. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide History Suggestions. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideHistorySuggestions FAQ Does it delete my history? No. It only stops history showing in suggestions. History → Show History… still has it all.

title: Hide New Tab Logo
text: Hides the Dia logo above the search field on new tab pages. Why use it If you want a plainer new tab page, this removes the logo and leaves the search field. It only hides the logo. The search field stays where it was, so there's an empty space above it. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide New Tab Logo. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideNewTabLogo FAQ Does the search field move? No. It stays where it was, with the space above it left empty.

title: Turn Off AI
text: Turns off every AI feature in Dia and cuts it off from its AI servers, so Dia works as a plain browser. Why use it If you never use Dia's AI, it's still in a dozen places: a Chat button in the toolbar, Chats in the sidebar, a Chat suggestion every time you type in the command bar, Ask Dia when you right-click, shortcuts you can hit by accident, whole panes in Settings, and more. This one switch takes all of them away at once, and stops Dia talking to its AI servers behind them. Skip it if you use chat even now and then; the separate Hide tweaks let you pick and choose. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Turn Off AI. Or run: sh diatweaks enable turnOffAI Dia asks to relaunch: it can only be cut off from its AI servers as it starts. Turning it off asks again, so chat can reach them. To send questions you type to your search engine as well, open Dia → Settings → Advanced and set Address Bar to Prefer Search Engine. What it hides - The Chat button in the toolbar, and Personalize. - The Chats button in the sidebar or tab bar. - Skills under the search field on new tab pages. - In the command bar: the Chat suggestion, ⌃⌘↩, Add tabs or files, and the "Looking for chat?" banner. "Ask anything…" becomes "Search or enter address". - File → Chat…, New Chat, Focus Chat, Send Chat Prompt Now, Open Daily Brief and Dia → Personalize Dia, with their shortcuts, including ones you set in Dia's Shortcuts settings. - Chat With This Tab, when you right-click a tab and on the card when you point at one. - Ask Dia about… when you right-click selected text. - In Settings: the Apps and Skills panes, Morning Brief, the Chat events and Daily report sounds, and the chat shortcuts. Chat beside the page closes if it's open, and closes again if anything opens it. What it blocks After a relaunch, Dia can't reach the servers behind chat, its web results, AI apps and skills, and artifacts. Anything that asks them fails at once, as if you were offline. Your account and subscription still work, and websites you visit aren't affected. Turn it off and relaunch, and they all come back. FAQ Does it make Dia use less memory? Not by much. Dia's AI code is still loaded; it just can't show anything or reach its servers. What about Hide Chat Button and the other Hide tweaks? They're in the same AI section, and still work on their own. With this on, they're greyed out: what they hide stays hidden whether they're on or off. Is Chat with Support still there? Yes. It's how you reach Dia's support team, so Help → Chat with Support stays.

title: Hide Chat Button
text: Hides the Chat button at the top right of the toolbar. Tabs in the sidebar Tabs at the top :---::---: Why use it If you don't use Chat, the button is a permanent bit of clutter at the toolbar's corner, and easy to click by accident. - Handy if you want a quieter toolbar. - Chat is still in the menu, so nothing is lost. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Chat Button. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideChatButton Works with While Hide Toolbar is on, the button is hidden with the rest of the toolbar and this switch is greyed out in Settings. With Show Toolbar on Hover too, the button stays hidden when the toolbar shows, as long as this tweak is on. FAQ Can I still use Chat? Yes. This only hides the button. Chat is still in Dia's File menu.

title: Hide Chats Button
text: Hides the Chats button at the bottom of the sidebar, or in the tab bar when tabs are at the top. Tabs in the sidebar Tabs at the top :---::---: Why use it If you don't use Chat history, the Chats button is clutter in the sidebar or tab bar. - Handy if you want a quieter bottom of the sidebar. - Skip it if you open past chats from there. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Chats Button. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideChatsButton

title: Hide Upgrade Banner
text: Hides the "Looking for chat? Upgrade to Better Days." banner that Dia shows under the command bar as you type, if your account has no chat usage left. Why use it If your account has no chat usage, the command bar keeps showing an upgrade offer as you type. This hides it so only your suggestions are left. It does nothing if you have chat usage. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Upgrade Banner. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideUpgradeBanner FAQ Why don't I see a difference? Dia only shows the banner to accounts without chat usage. With chat usage there's nothing to hide. What about Command bar? Command bar doesn't show the banner either way: it sits under the new tab page, which Command bar hides.

title: Hide Personalize Button
text: Hides the "Personalization on for new chats" button at the top right of new tab pages. Why use it If you don't use chat personalization, the button at the top right of the new tab page is clutter. This hides it. It has no effect while Hide Toolbar is on, because that already hides the toolbar the button sits in. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Personalize Button. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hidePersonalizeButton

title: Hide Skills Suggestions
text: Hides the Skills and Learn Skills buttons under the search field on new tab pages. Why use it The Skills and Learn Skills buttons take up space on the new tab page. If you don't use skills, or want the page to show only the search field, this hides them. Skills still work from elsewhere in Dia. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Hide Skills Suggestions. Or run: sh diatweaks enable hideSkillsSuggestions FAQ Can I still use skills? Yes. This only hides the buttons on new tab pages.

title: Window Material
text: Puts a macOS material or Liquid Glass behind the tabs and sidebar, still tinted with your profile's color, so they pick up what is behind the window. Why use it Dia's window is a flat color. If you like the translucent look other Mac apps have, this gives Dia the same, and you can pick from every material and Liquid Glass style macOS has. Handy when you want Dia to match macOS 26 or a wallpaper you like. Skip it if you want text on the sidebar to stay as high contrast as possible, since translucent materials let busy backgrounds show through. Turn it on Open Dia → Settings → Patches and switch on Window Material. Or run: sh diatweaks enable windowMaterial Pick the material on the same page, under Options → Material. It's Abutted Sidebar glass to begin with. Every material Each one in light and dark mode, with no other tweaks on. Light Dark --------- Dia's own, with the tweak off Titlebar Menu Popover Sidebar Header HUD Window Full Screen UI Tooltip Under Window Background Every Liquid Glass Liquid Glass needs macOS 26. Light Dark --------- Regular Clear Dock App Icons Widgets Text AV Player FaceTime Control Center Notification Center Monogram Bubbles Identity Focus Border Focus Platter Keyboard Sidebar Abutted Sidebar Inspector Control Loupe Slider Camera Cartouche Popover FAQ What can I pick? Every material macOS offers apps, such as Sidebar, Popover and HUD Window, and on macOS 26 every kind of Liquid Glass macOS has, including ones it keeps for itself, like Dock, Control Center and Abutted Sidebar. A few, like Sidebar, are nearly solid in light mode. Every one is pictured above. Why does the new tab page look like glass too? It has no background of its own, so it shows the window's.
